messages:
sophie: quick heads-up — I have a small repro for the Go SDK where cancelling the context mid-stream seems to leave the client pinned and partial JSON fragments pile up. not a full leak but backpressure spikes. logs attached below.

liam: oh interesting. does it only happen when the server splits objects across SSE 'data:' frames?

sophie: yes, fragmented objects + server-side keepalive. reproduction steps: 1) start small test server that emits a 2k JSON chunk split into 3 'data:' frames with 50ms gaps, 2) client uses http.Client + bufio.NewReader(resp.Body).ReadBytes('\n'), 3) cancel ctx after first token processed. observed: goroutines reading still waiting and the buffered fragments accumulate.

maria: can you paste the minimal client read loop?

sophie: sure — gist of it: ```go
req = http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "GET", url, nil)
resp, _ := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
r := bufio.NewReader(resp.Body)
for {
    line, err := r.ReadBytes('\n') // expecting "data: {..}\n"
    if err != nil { break }
    // assemble JSON chunks on 'data:' lines, unmarshal when 'data:' == "[DONE]"
}
resp.Body.Close()
```

liam: hitting ReadBytes after ctx cancel can block until the server sends more bytes. Close() of resp.Body should unblock but only if the underlying transport sees EOF. sometimes net/http with http2 won't return until window update?

jon: we saw similar with our net/http + keepalive earlier. potential fixes: 1) set resp.Body's ReadDeadline via conn (harder with net/http), 2) use a custom Transport with DialContext and set deadlines, 3) track a cancel channel and explicitly Close() the response body in a goroutine when ctx.Done(). which did you try?

sophie: I tried goroutine that calls resp.Body.Close() on ctx.Done() — it helps but doesn't always free the ReadBytes call immediately under heavy load. behavior seems worse when server deliberately sends very short fragments (split inside multibyte utf8).

maria: could be a partial-utf8 split causing bufio to wait for continuation bytes before returning a full rune and ReadBytes waiting for delimiter. try ReadSlice('\n') instead of ReadBytes? ReadSlice still returns partial if delimiter found. also consider using resp.Body.Read into a fixed buffer and handle framing yourself (faster and gives you control).

liam: another approach — switch to a non-blocking parse: use io.Pipe and copy in a separate goroutine that monitors ctx. minimal pattern: the reading goroutine loops on resp.Body.Read into []byte; parser goroutine consumes from pipe.Reader and builds events. When ctx cancels, Close() pipe writer and resp.Body. That usually wakes readers.

jon: note re: auth refresh race — our SDK's auth middleware refreshes token mid-stream and briefly rewrites Authorization header then retries the entire request for 401. if a 401 happens while we're in the middle of a long-lived SSE, the retry path may leave old body readers dangling. ensure auth retry path only triggers for non-streaming endpoints or does a graceful handoff.

sophie: good call. in my repro I toggled token expiry and saw a quick 401 then that seems to correlate with the stuck reader. maybe auth refresh triggered transport reuse weirdness.

maria: small patch idea: for streaming endpoints we should avoid automatic request-level retries. add a transport flag SkipRetriesForStreams and a heuristic: if Content-Type is text/event-stream or the request has header X-Redwood-Streaming: 1, then disable retries. we can fallback to a lightweight 2xx->fallback model.

liam: agree. also add instrumentation: metric for "streaming_read_block_ms" per request and a trace that captures ctx cancellations + resp.Body.Close() calls to see ordering.

sophie: I sketched a PR that: a) disables auth retries for streaming, b) adds goroutine that closes resp.Body on ctx.Done(), c) switches parsing loop to ReadSlice and a manual utf8.AppendRune-safe assembly. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go/pull/1234 — could someone glance? small tests included.

jon: pinged review. quick question: does the PR add a special header for streams?

sophie: yes, sets X-Redwood-Streaming: 1 in client for streaming endpoints. will update docs.

dev-bot: CI started for PR #1234 — go test ./... (15m estimated) :gear: 

liam: thanks. if CI is flaky, I can run the repro in a loop on my laptop. otherwise lgtm as long as we add a comment in the auth middleware explaining why retries are off for streams.

maria: also add a tiny e2e that simulates fragmented utf8 and confirm ctx cancel unblocks within 200ms.

sophie: added both tests and the comment. I'll merge after CI green and one more review. thanks all :thumbsup:
